text: I could wish that you would say, to the five or six men or women with whom you are the most acquainted, that you are sensible that, from youth and inexperience, you must make many mistakes in good-breeding; that you beg of them to correct you, without reserve, wherever they see you fail; and that you shall take such admonition as the strongest proofs of their friendship.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CI, to his son, London, January 11, Old Style 1750
